crop.notes: A Hambrick & Co. book-betting notice at the top, then the Tom Allen 'Sporting Notes' notice, then an unrelated story, 'A Narrow Escape', about a falling stone on North Fourth Street.

ocr.notes: The Allen notice is read correctly apart from small errors ('cf', 'eo-gaged').

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat carried a notice for Tom Allen, retired champion pugilist of the world, at 619 Market Street, with a free concert every evening and only the best singers engaged.

metadata.notes: The masthead is too small to read on the scaled page; the page's dispatches are dated August 15, which fits an August 16, 1890 paper.

facts.fact: Allen, billed as retired champion pugilist of the world, ran his saloon at 619 Market Street with a free concert every evening and only the best singers engaged

notes: Recrop to the 'Sporting Notes' item; the betting notice and the falling-stone story are not about Allen.
